images.title: Three beams, three nails
images.purpose: Show a triangle as three beams joined at three corner nails, so vertices and sides are clear.
images.composition: One large triangular roof frame in the centre on white space, with nothing else around it.
exact_structure: Three straight beams drawn as thick amber (#E69F00) bars forming a closed triangle with a flat base at the bottom and the apex at the top centre.
Exactly three round dark nail dots, one at each corner of the triangle: apex, bottom left, bottom right.
The corners are labelled A at the apex, B at the bottom left and C at the bottom right.
No other objects, no ground, no people.
rejection: more or fewer than three beams or three nails
the triangle is open at any corner
labels anywhere other than A top, B bottom left, C bottom right
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A triangle has three corner points (vertices) and three sides that join them.
images.description: A triangle frame made of three beams joined by three nails labelled A, B and C.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to point to the three vertices and then the three sides.

image_decisions.why: The hook needs the three vertices and three sides in view before asking what happens when they lie on a line.
